summary: Richard Hauschild (1901–1972) worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Tübingen, Leipzig under Johannes Hertel, and Jena under Albert Debrunner. He held posts as Lektor (1938) and Professor (1951–1967) at the University of Jena.

Richard Henebry (1863–1916) was a scholar in linguistics and other fields. He studied at St. John's College, Waterford, St Patrick's Pontifical University, the University of Greifswald under Heinrich Zimmer, and the University of Freiburg.

Richard Hugh Robinson (1926–1970) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at the University of Alberta, SOAS, and the University of London under David Snellgrove, Arthur Waley, and David Friedman. He became a professor at Wisconsin-Madison in 1961.

Richard Hughes Seager (b. 1948) works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Wisconsin System, Harvard Divinity School, and Harvard University (PhD), and served as Associate Professor of Religion at Hamilton College around 1994.

Richard J. Davidson (b. 1951) studied at Midwood High School, New York University, and Harvard University. He was a psychology professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison from 2001 to 2017, having also held posts there in 1987 and 1996.

Richard Jay Kohn (d. 2000) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison by 1988, studying under doctoral supervisor Geshe Lhundub Sopa and traditional teacher Lama Tharchin Rinpoche.

Richard K. Payne (b. 1949) is a Buddhist studies and Japanology scholar who studied under Chisei Aratano and Taisen Miyata. Around 1996, he was Dean at the Institute of Buddhist Studies and Core Doctoral Faculty at the Graduate Theological Union.

Richard Keith Sprigg (1922–2011) was a scholar of linguistics and Tibetology. After attending Oakham School from around 1936 to 1940, he held appointments at the University of London and SOAS University of London from circa 1948 to 1980.

Richard Kieckhefer (b. 1946), a history and religious studies scholar, studied at Saint Louis University, University of Texas at Austin, and Monumenta Germaniae Historica. In 1975, he became Professor of History and John Evans Professor of Religious Studies at Northwestern University.

Richard King (b. 1965) specializes in religious studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at Dalhousie, McGill, and Lancaster under Daniel Mariau, later holding posts at Stirling (~1996–2000), Vanderbilt (~2005–2011), and Glasgow (~2011–2013).

Richard M. Jaffe (b. 1954) specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He held a post at North Carolina State University (~1995–2000) before serving as Professor of Religious Studies at Duke University around 2000.

Richard Mahoney works in Buddhist studies and computational fields. He earned his Master of Arts at the University of Canterbury by 2002 under the supervision of Paul Harrison, and was affiliated with the university around 2001.

Richard Morris (1833–1894) was an Indology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies scholar who attended Battersea Training College. He taught English at King's College School (1869) and served as headmaster at the Royal Masonic School for Boys (1875–1888).

Richard N. Frye (1920–2014) worked in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Illinois Urbana-Champaign and Harvard, serving in the Office of Strategic Services (~1942–1945) and on Harvard's faculty from circa 1948 to 1990.

Richard P. Boyle completed graduate studies at the University of Washington and studied under traditional teacher Kyozan Joshu Sasaki. He taught at the University of California, Los Angeles, and held a post at the University of New Mexico in 2015.

Richard P. Hayes (b. 1945) is an Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed his doctorate at Toronto under Bimal Krishna Matilal, later teaching at Toronto, McGill University (attested 1997–2009), and the University of New Mexico (attested 2011–2016).

Richard Payne is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He served as Dean at the Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 1996, 2007) and held a post at the University of Chicago (attested 2021).

Richard Phené Spiers (1838–1916) was an archaeology and history scholar. He studied at King's College London from around 1854 to 1858 and at the École Nationale Supérieure des Beaux-Arts from around 1858 to 1861.

Richard Pischel (1849–1908) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Breslau under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler and at Berlin under Albrecht Weber. He held professorships at Kiel (1875), Halle (1885–1902), and Berlin (1902–1908).

Richard Polenberg (1937–2020) was a historian who studied at Brooklyn College and Columbia University. He was a Professor of American History at Cornell University from 1966 to 2011 and also served as a Fulbright Visiting Professor at Hebrew University.
